drivingQuestion: From where do we know that the first Pesach requires hallel at its eating and the second does not?
outcomeNote: The source is Isaiah 30:29 via R. Yoḥanan citing R. Shimon ben Yehotzadak.

segments.he: הָרִאשׁוֹן טָעוּן הַלֵּל בַּאֲכִילָתוֹ וְכוּ׳. מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק: אָמַר קְרָא ״הַשִּׁיר יִהְיֶה לָכֶם כְּלֵיל הִתְקַדֶּשׁ חָג״. לַיְלָה הַמְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג — טָעוּן הַלֵּל, לַיְלָה שֶׁאֵין מְקוּדָּשׁ לֶחָג — אֵין טָעוּן הַלֵּל.
segments.en: It was taught in the mishna that the Paschal lamb on «the first» Pesaḥ «requires» the recitation of «hallel as it is eaten,» whereas on the second Pesaḥ it does not. The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «Rabbi Yoḥanan said, citing Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak,» that «the verse states: “You shall have a song as in the night when a Festival is sanctified”» (Isaiah 30:29). From here it may be derived that «a night sanctified as a Festival,» on which labor is prohibited, such as the first night of Passover, «requires» the recitation of «hallel;» however, «a night which is not sanctified as a Festival,» such as the night when the Paschal lamb is eaten following the second Pesaḥ, «does not require» the recitation of «hallel.»
